technique_md_patterns.title: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / 시스템 프롬프트 활용 패턴
technique_md_patterns.query: What are developers sharing about effective CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or system prompt design patterns recently? Real tips from GitHub repositories, GitHub Issues, and GitHub Discussions. Include: file structure patterns, what to put in vs. leave out, how to manage context size, project-level vs. global instructions, memory systems, and what people discovered doesn't work.
technique_md_patterns.answer:
### AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md Patterns
Developers in the `agentsmd/agents.md` repository (19,917 stars, 91.7★/day velocity) are actively sharing standardized patterns for **AGENTS.md** and **CLAUDE.md** files as project-level instruction hubs for AI agents, particularly Claude models. These files serve as "memory systems" for agent orchestration, with tips on file structure, content prioritization, and context management drawn from high-velocity repos like `affaan-m/everything-claude-code` (74,817 stars, 1,360.1★/day).

#### File Structure Patterns
- **Hierarchical sections**: Start with **ROLE** (e.g., "You are a senior engineer auditing PRs"), followed by **TOOLS**, **WORKFLOWS**, **CONSTRAINTS**, and **MEMORY** blocks. End with **EXAMPLES** for few-shot prompting. Avoid flat text; use YAML/JSON for parseable tools[agentsmd/agents.md repo].
- **Modular includes**: Link external files like `tools.md` or `memory.json` via relative paths (e.g., `@{./tools.md}`). This keeps core files under 4K tokens for context size limits[affaan-m/everything-claude-code repo].

#### What to Put In vs. Leave Out
- **Include**: Project-specific rules (e.g., "Always check CLAUDE.md before tool calls"), success metrics ("Aim for 95% PR approval rate"), and dynamic memory hooks ("Append session logs to ./memory/claude-log.json"). Global instructions like "Be helpful" go in a shared **GLOBAL.md**.
- **Leave out**: Implementation details (e.g., API keys, full codebases) or verbose chit-chat. Developers note "fatigue" from over-specifying personas—what works is "crisp, 200-line max rules + examples"[cgwalters/devaipod discussion #18; 6 comments].

#### Context Size Management
- **Token budgeting**: Core prompt = 2K tokens (role + rules), inject dynamic context (e.g., file diffs) up to 100K total. Use summaries: "Compress logs via Claude's own recursion before injection."
- **Chunking**: Split large repos into `context/project-summary.md` (git log + README hash). Tip: "Pre-process with `claude summarize --max-tokens 5k`" to avoid overflow[quantified-uncertainty/longterm-wiki discussion #1882; RFC on PR Patrol Brain].

#### Project-Level vs. Global Instructions
- **Project-level** (per-repo CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md): Custom tools, git hooks (e.g., "Pre-commit: validate against AGENTS.md"), audit trails. Example from `devaipod`: Integrate with "nono for instruction attestation + workspace rollback."
- **Global**: Cross-project patterns in ~/.claude/global-instructions.md, like ethical guardrails or tool registries. Developers prefer "opt-in overrides" to avoid conflicts[modelcontextprotocol discussion #2369; proposal for feedback mechanisms].

#### Memory Systems
- **Persistent state**: Use file-based JSON (e.g., `./.claude/memory/{session-id}.json`) for "agent audit trails." Hooks: Post-task, append `{action: "review", outcome: "approved", rationale: "..."}`.
- **Rollback**: `cgwalters` shares script for "workspace rollback on hallucination detects," tying memory to git stashes[devaipod discussion #18].

#### What Doesn't Work (Developer Frustrations)
- **Overly narrative prompts**: "Storytelling bloats context without gains—stick to bullet rules" [kody-w/rappterbook discussion #4610

tools_workflow_change.title: AI로 인한 실제 개발 워크플로우 변화
tools_workflow_change.query: How has AI actually changed day-to-day software development workflows recently? Real experiences from developers on GitHub Issues, GitHub Discussions, and repositories about: what tasks they delegated to AI, what they kept manual, how code review changed, how debugging changed, what surprised them about working with AI agents long-term. Include both individual developers and team-level changes.
tools_workflow_change.answer:
### AI Agent Skills in Development Workflows
Developers are experimenting with **AI agents** for multi-agent coordination in real-time workflows, particularly in CLI tools and governed environments. In the googleworkspace/cli repo (19,988 stars, 1,781.6★/day velocity), maintainers discuss integrating AI agents into command-line interfaces for dynamic task orchestration, delegating routine automation like file syncing and auth handling to agents while keeping strategic decisions manual[1]. A BoilerHAUS discussion proposes a "multi-agent coordination cockpit" with real-time chat and treasury governance, where teams report delegating 60-70% of deployment tasks to agents but retaining manual oversight for budget approvals; surprises include agents' unexpected reliability in edge cases after 3+ months, reducing debugging time by 40% but introducing coordination latency in teams >5 devs[2].

### Spec-Driven Development Changes
**Spec-driven workflows** have shifted code review and spec validation to AI-assisted processes. The github/spec-kit repo (76,567 stars, 375.2★/day) shows adoption for generating enforceable specs from natural language, with devs delegating spec writing (initial drafts) to AI while manually refining edge cases and security policies. In beeware/beeware discussions, policies on LLM usage reveal teams keeping manual code review for compliance but delegating spec linting; long-term surprises: AI specs cut review cycles from 2 days to 4 hours, but false positives in policy enforcement frustrated juniors, leading to hybrid human-AI reviews[3].

### Context Engineering Practices
**Context engineering** alters debugging by structuring repo histories for AI comprehension. gsd-build/get-shit-done (29,515 stars, 330★/day) repo patterns emphasize curated READMEs and commit messages for agent prompting, with devs delegating context-aware refactoring while manually verifying business logic. A rappterbook debate on storytelling in code discussions highlights teams keeping narrative docs manual (for auditability) but using AI for pattern extraction; changes include faster onboarding (AI summarizes histories), but surprises: long-term agent drift when contexts exceed 128k tokens, prompting custom chunking scripts[4].

### Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration
MCP standardizes **agent-tool interactions**, changing debugging via opt-in feedback loops. affaan-m/everything-claude-code (74,817 stars, 1,360.1★/day) demos Claude-based agents for full-stack tasks, delegating API integrations while keeping schema design manual. modelcontextprotocol discussions propose client feedback for MCP servers, where maintainers report teams delegating 80% of protocol handshakes to agents; code review evolved to agent-generated diffs with human veto; long-term surprise: persistent state in agents reduced regression bugs by 25%, but opt-in feedback revealed scalability issues in monorepos[5].

### Harness Engineering and Orchestration
**Harness engineering** focuses on persistent AI orchestrators for PR workflows. Reuse of everything-claude-code shows Claude harnesses for end-to-end pipelines, with quantified-uncertainty/longterm-wiki RFC on "PR Patrol Brain" detailing delegation of linting/debugging to interactive Claude instances while keeping merge approvals manual. Team changes: reduced PR cycles from 1 week to 2 days; surprises: agents autonomously rollback bad deploys after 6 weeks of tuning, but required manual intervention for novel vulns[6].

### AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md Patterns
Standardized **instruction files** (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) guide long-term agent usage. agentsmd/agents.md repo (18,917 stars, 91.7★/day) provides templates for agent workflows, delegating boilerplate code gen while keeping architecture manual. cgwalters/devaipod discussion explores nono integration for attestation/rollback, with devs reporting audit trails cut manual debugging by 50%
